question.worked_solution:
The roots of $f(w)$ are the solutions to the equation $f(w)=0.$ In our case, we have

$$
\frac{{w}^{2}-w-2}{w-5}=0.
$$

First, we factor $f(w),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(w) & =\frac{{w}^{2}-w-2}{w-5} \\  & =\frac{(w-2)(w+1)}{w-5}\end{aligned}
$$

There are no common factors in the numerator and denominator, so we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $w:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(w-2)(w+1) & =0 \\ w & =-1,\,2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions to $f(w)=0$ are $w=-1$ and $w=2.$
